name: Fire station
summary: Fire stations are essential-facility (Risk Category IV) buildings: tall long-span apparatus bays with heavy slabs and aprons, oversized bay doors, vehicle exhaust capture, decon/gear rooms, 24/7 living quarters and emergency generators, plus large paved site areas - so they price well above other civic buildings of similar size. Data is good: 2023-2026 public estimates and bid awards from TX, FL, MD, OH, CA and MA cluster at ~$420-$720/SF in low-cost states and ~$950-$1,000+/SF in CA/MA.

typicalSize.method: Recent projects: 7,900 SF (e4), 9,608 (e6), 12,195 (e1), 17,500 (e7), 17,877 (e3), 19,400 (e5), 20,619 (e2), ~20,000 (e8). Mid 15,000 SF = typical 3-bay career station with quarters for one shift.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building SF per site acre. Cameron Park assumes 3.0 acres for 12,195 SF (~4,065 SF/acre, e1). Drive-through bays need deep front and rear aprons plus staff/visitor parking and secured yard; 1.5-3 acres for 10-20k SF stations gives ~3,500-10,000 SF/acre.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per SF of building (= 1.2-3.0 per 1,000 SF). Sized for two overlapping shifts plus visitors/training: ~20-35 spaces for a 15,000 SF station. Derived; local code governs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard cost incl. sitework per SF of building. 2023-2026 evidence: TX $420 (e4), $460 (e2, 2023), $719 (e3); MD $503 (e5); OH $503-$628 (e7); FL $652-$678 (e6); Northeast avg $705 (e9); CA $951 (e1); MA ~$1,015 (e8). Median of these nine anchors ~ $680; because the upper anchors are high-cost CA/MA markets (national-equivalent ~$750-$800), the national mid is set lower at $625/SF in 2025 dollars. Low $425 = small/simple rural station in a low-cost market (e4); high $950 = CA/MA-level pricing or heavy program (e1, e8). Older rules of thumb ($275-$400 in 2017, e10; RSMeans 2019 ~$160-$183 building-only, e11/e12) are retained as evidence but sit well below current bids.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions and OH&P, apparatus apron, on-site paving/utilities/landscaping, fixed bay equipment (exhaust capture, gear extractor); excludes land, soft costs, loose FF&E, station alerting/IT where owner-furnished, off-site improvements, impact/tap fees.

qualityTiers.method: Economy ~ pre-engineered metal bay with simple CMU quarters (e4/e5 ~$420-$503 vs. $625 mid); premium/luxury ~ masonry, two-story, training features, high-performance/net-zero (Williamstown in e9 was adjusted for net-zero design) at 1.25-1.5x.

systemSplit.method: Derived. Site share (31+32+33 = 15%) anchored on Cameron Park site & civil $1.9M of $11.6M hard (16%, e1); Div 01 ~8% from West University Place GC conditions 3.5% + fee 5.5% (e2). Electrical set as the largest trade (12%, incl. generator/ATS) per Firehouse ('biggest expense ... is electrical, followed by site work', e10). Openings 7% reflect 4-fold/overhead apparatus doors; Div 11 3% = exhaust capture, extractors, kitchen. Remaining splits follow a typical masonry/steel municipal building.

lineItems.name: Vehicle exhaust capture system (per apparatus bay)

cost.method: Derived allowance for a source-capture (hose rail) system per drive-through bay; Firehouse notes exhaust systems 'have become standard in new fire stations' (e10). Verify with vendor quote.

lineItems.notes: Qty = number of apparatus bays (3 typical; Terrell, Hernando and Corpus Christi stations are all 3-bay, e3/e6/e14).

lineItems.name: Apparatus bay doors - 4-fold or high-speed sectional (per door)

cost.method: Derived: insulated overhead sectional doors at the low end, 4-fold bi-fold doors at the high end; 2 doors per drive-through bay.

lineItems.notes: 6 doors = 3 drive-through bays x front and rear. Inside Div 08 share.

lineItems.name: Emergency standby generator + ATS (100% station load)

cost.method: Derived allowance for a 150-400 kW diesel/natural-gas genset with ATS, pad and enclosure; essential-facility stations must stay operational (e8).

lineItems.name: Turnout gear extractor/dryer and decon room fit-out

cost.method: Derived allowance: commercial gear washer-extractor(s), drying cabinet, decon sinks/showers.

lineItems.notes: Contamination-reduction ('hot zone') design is now standard.

lineItems.name: Station alerting / dispatch interface and IT

cost.method: Derived allowance; often owner-furnished through the dispatch/IT budget.

lineItems.notes: Add when not carried in the owner's technology budget.

lineItems.name: Training tower / drill prop (masonry, 3-4 stories)

cost.method: Derived allowance; Green Valley Station 25 includes a 3-story masonry training tower in its $9.76M award (e5) but the tower is not priced separately.

lineItems.notes: Optional program element; headquarters stations only.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Firehouse soft-cost guidance: FF&E 'target budget of $15-$30 per square foot of the facility' (e13); mid = midpoint.

pctOfHard.method: Cameron Park carries soft costs at ~25% of construction incl. FF&E and owner contingency (e1); Firehouse 2017 'another 25 percent' (e10); Firehouse 2020 10%-30% of project budget (e13). Excluding FF&E and contingency: West University Place soft cost $1.247M on $9.49M construction = 13% (e2); Tyngsborough final design + OPM $2.72M on $20.3M = 13.4% (+ $0.3M schematic design, e8). Mid 20% of hard (pure soft, ex-FF&E/contingency, incl. design, PM/OPM, permits, testing, builder's risk, commissioning).

softCosts.notes: A/E 6.13%-9.21% of construction for a ~$5M station (e13); testing 0.25%-0.75%; builder's risk ~1%; commissioning $1.20-$3.50/SF. Many states require an OPM/CM for public buildings (MA, e8).

design.method: West University Place carries 5% design contingency at concept (e2); Tyngsborough 10% at schematic design (e8); RFM: 20% is not uncommon at the earliest stage (e16).

hard.method: Hernando County Station 15 contract carries a $250k owner's contingency = ~4% (e6); Firehouse: owner contingency 3%-8% of budget (e13).

soft.method: Derived; West University Place carries a separate 6% owner contingency (e2) and RFM recommends tapering to 5%-10% (e16).

perPrimaryUnit.method: All-in (hard + soft, excl. land) per building SF: low ~ $420 hard (e4) x ~1.1-1.15; high ~ Tyngsborough $24.8M / ~20,000 SF = ~$1,240 (e8) and Missoula's $16.5M/14,000 SF (~$1,180, in 2028 dollars); allow to $1,400 for CA/MA headquarters stations.

source.title: Fire Station Budgeting and Cost Control

evidence.quote: It would not be uncommon to budget 20% at the early stage of a project.
evidence.scopeNotes: Early-stage owner contingency (as % of hard+soft), reduced to 5-10% over the project. Also: 'soft costs can easily total 25% of your hard costs, and can sometimes be as high as 50%'.

openQuestions: Broadview Heights OH estimate (e7) is a scanned PDF and is cited via a secondary article; verify against the city document.
No sourced per-bay costs for exhaust capture, bay doors, generator or alerting - all line items are derived allowances; vendor quotes would firm them up.
A national fire-station $/SF survey (e.g., Firehouse Station Design Awards data book) would let the mid be set from a larger sample than nine projects.
